public_rationale: The contract reads the claim as saying generative AI had not created a meaningful number of new jobs from January 2023 to July 8, 2024. Indeed Hiring Lab reported that GenAI-related postings grew more than 30-fold from January 2023 to the end of February 2024 (e1). They reached 11 in 10,000 US postings, which Indeed called 'a very small share' (e1). In March 2024, Indeed's economists wrote that GenAI and AI tools were 'already creating new jobs' (e2). They gave no count of net new jobs. Postings that mention GenAI are not shown to be net new roles rather than existing jobs that now mention it. OpenAI said it had about 1,200 employees in April 2024 (e3). That is hiring at one company, not an economy-wide measure. The evidence shows some GenAI-related hiring. It does not measure net new jobs caused by generative AI, and the claim sets no threshold for 'meaningful'. So the evidence neither confirms nor refutes the claim.
limitations: Posting shares are not employment counts.
The posting data come from one job board, Indeed.
The Indeed data end in February 2024 and do not cover March to July 2024.
Indeed's statement that GenAI was creating jobs comes with no net or economy-wide count.
No source in the packet sets a threshold for how many jobs would be 'meaningful'.

statement.excerpt: the sense that generative AI will create new jobs (it hasn't in 18 months)

from_speaker: the sense that generative AI will create new jobs
our_interpretation: Plain reading: in the roughly 18 months from the generative AI boom (ChatGPT, late 2022) to the post, generative AI has not created a meaningful number of new jobs across the economy. He is rebutting hype about job creation in the labour market, so a handful of hires at AI startups would not count against him.
Target period: January 2023 to the post date, about 18 months back from July 2024.
'Meaningful' has no threshold in his words. Gross job postings that mention generative AI are not the same as net new jobs caused by it.
criteria.support_condition: Labour-market data for 2023 to mid-2024 showing no material net job creation that can be traced to generative AI, for example GenAI-linked roles too few to register in employment totals and no new occupations at scale.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Labour-market data for 2023 to mid-2024 showing a material number of new jobs created because of generative AI, beyond relabelled existing roles, at a scale an informed reader would call meaningful.

evidence.explanation: GenAI-related postings grew fast but stayed at about 0.11% of US postings. That is real but small, and postings that mention GenAI are not shown to be net new jobs, so this neither clearly meets nor clearly fails a 'meaningful job creation' test.
